turnaround_reason: Capri was beaten down after the failed Tapestry merger and years of Michael Kors declines. It has since sold Versace to Prada for $1.4B, slashed net debt from ~$1.5B to ~$224M, and is early in a Michael Kors reset (fewer SKUs, less promotion, new handbag icons) with Michael Kors full-price comps turning positive for the first time in several quarters.
bullish_points: Balance sheet transformed: net debt cut from ~$1.5B to ~$224M via the $1.4B Versace sale to Prada
Operational green shoots: Michael Kors full-price comps turned positive in Q2; Jimmy Choo growth path toward ~$800M revenue
CEO John Idol bought 55,000 shares (~$989K) — a real recent insider signal; dossier shows net insider buying of ~634K shares over 6 months
Cheap at forward P/E ~6.1; active takeover interest with potential buyers reported circling
Liquid options (ATM IV ~67%) allow defined-risk expressions of the M&A/turnaround bet
bearish_points: 12-month insider activity is net selling despite the recent CEO purchase; signal is mixed
Michael Kors turnaround is early and accessible-luxury demand is fragile
Reported debt/equity is extreme (lease-distorted) and the business is still cyclical
20% below the 200d MA — the basing thesis is unconfirmed and could re-break down if M&A talks fizzle
catalyst: A takeover bid/sale-process outcome, and continued positive Michael Kors comps confirming the operational reset
catalyst_timing: M&A process ongoing (near-term, next 1-2 quarters); Q4 FY2026 and next-quarter comps
suggested_trade: Spot core position plus a defined-risk call spread into the M&A/turnaround catalyst; size for a binary sale-process outcome
key_risk: The sale process ends with no deal and Michael Kors comps roll back over, removing both catalysts at once
would_skip_if: M&A speculation fully deflates and comps turn negative again; the thesis leans meaningfully on the deal optionality
